# Friedreich ataxia

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Neurology > Movement disorders > Friedreich ataxia*

[Original Article Link](/library/KR0ULf)

---

## Summary

Friedreich <u>ataxia</u> (FDRA) is an <u>autosomal recessive</u> disorder involving <u>trinucleotide repeat expansion</u> that leads to progressive neurodegeneration. It affects multiple <u>spinal cord tracts</u>, causing <u>muscle weakness</u> and impaired coordination of all limbs. A staggering gait in childhood is the resulting main symptom. Other features include skeletal abnormalities, <u>cardiomyopathy</u>, and <u>diabetes</u>. The clinical course is mainly determined by the extent of the loss of mobility and cardiac involvement. Diagnosis requires confirmation with genetic tests. Because there is no curative therapy available, the prognosis is poor.

## Epidemiology

* The most common <u>autosomal recessive</u> <u>ataxia</u> [[1]](/library/DSX1bB)

* Peak <u>incidence</u>: 8–15 years (most cases < 25 years)  [[2]](/library/wSXhbB)[[3]](/library/ySXdXB)

* Affects individuals of Central and Northern European descent  [[2]](/library/wSXhbB)




Epidemiological data refers to the US, unless otherwise specified.

---

## Etiology

* <u>Trinucleotide repeat expansion</u> (of the <u>nucleotide</u> triplet GAA) in the FXN <u>gene</u> on <u>chromosome</u> 9;  → deficiency of <u>frataxin</u> (an <u>iron</u>-binding protein) → intramitochondrial accumulation of <u>iron</u> and ; dysregulation of cellular antioxidant defense due to <u>mitochondrial</u> dysfunction → oxidative damage and degeneration of <u>CNS</u> and <u>PNS</u>




References: [[2]](/library/wSXhbB)[[4]](/library/COYqu6)

---

## Clinical features

* Neurological

* Progressive <u>ataxia</u> (impaired coordination of muscles) of all limbs  ;  due to damage to the <u>spinocerebellar tracts</u> (often a presenting feature)

* <u>Gait ataxia</u>

* Bilateral lower limbs equally affected

* Wide-based gait with frequent falling

* Titubation while standing or sitting

* Arms: action and <u>intention tremor</u>s

* Associated symptoms

* Impaired <u>proprioception</u> and <u>vibration sense</u> (<u>pallhypesthesia</u>) due to damage to the <u>dorsal columns</u>

* Loss of <u>deep tendon reflexes</u> due to degeneration of the <u>dorsal root ganglia</u>

* <u>Spastic paralysis</u> due to degeneration of the <u>lateral corticospinal tract</u>

* <u>Nystagmus</u>

* <u>Dysarthria</u> and <u>dysphagia</u> (may be accompanied by uncoordinated breathing)

* <u>Bladder</u> dysfunction

* <u>Hearing loss</u>

* Skeletal deformities

* Secondary <u>scoliosis</u> (<u>kyphoscoliosis</u>): usually occurs in childhood

* <u>Foot deformity</u>: <u>foot inversion</u> (<u>talipes equinovarus</u>) and/or high-arched foot (<u>pes cavus</u>) with <u>hammertoes</u>

* Other features

* Concentric <u>hypertrophic cardiomyopathy</u>: <u>palpitations</u>, <u>arrhythmias</u>, <u>dyspnea</u>, exercise intolerance  [[5]](/library/x_cEqU0)

* <u>Diabetes mellitus</u>

* <u>Personality</u> changes (e.g., emotional lability)





> [!NOTE]
> Individuals with FRiedreich ATAXia have ATAXic GAAit due to the expansion of the triplet GAA in the FRATAXin <u>gene</u>.

---

## Diagnosis

* A specific <u>trinucleotide repeat expansion</u> assay should be performed in all suspected cases.

* <u>ECG</u>: <u>T-wave</u> <u>inversion</u> and ventricular <u>hypertrophy</u>

* <u>Echocardiography</u>: symmetric, concentric ventricular <u>hypertrophy</u>

* <u>Nerve conduction studies</u>

* Sensory: absent or reduced sensory nerve <u>action potentials</u> (SNAP)

* Motor: normal until advanced stages

* <u>MRI</u> <u>brain</u> and spinal cord: <u>cervical spine</u> <u>atrophy</u> (minimal <u>cerebellar</u> <u>atrophy</u>)





References:[[4]](/library/COYqu6)

---

## Treatment

* No curative treatment available

* Multidisciplinary <u>supportive care</u>: <u>genetic counseling</u>, <u>physiotherapy</u>, and <u>speech and language therapy</u>

* Treatment of cardiologic, orthopedic, and metabolic (i.e., <u>diabetes</u>) features of the disease





References:[[4]](/library/COYqu6)

---

## Prognosis

* Nonambulation is common by age 20–30.

* Average age at <u>death</u>: 37 years

* <u>Causes of death</u>

* Most common: <u>heart failure</u> due to <u>hypertrophic cardiomyopathy</u>

* Respiratory complications





References:[[6]](/library/zParhk)
